title: Error FLX-401: sync token expired
text: Error FLX-401 indicates the synchronization token has expired. Fluxline issues sync tokens with a 24-hour TTL. To resolve, rotate the token from Settings > Connections > Regenerate Token, then restart the affected connector. Recurring FLX-401 errors usually indicate a clock-skew problem on the agent host; verify NTP is enabled.

title: Error FLX-503: upstream connector unavailable
text: FLX-503 is raised when the upstream connector cannot be reached for more than 60 seconds. Check the connector health dashboard first. If the upstream system is healthy, inspect egress firewall rules — Fluxline agents require outbound TCP 443 to *.fluxline.io. FLX-503 during scheduled maintenance windows can be suppressed with maintenance mode.

title: Configuring SSO with SAML 2.0
text: Fluxline supports single sign-on (SSO) via SAML 2.0. Configure your identity provider with the ACS URL from Admin > Security > SSO. Attribute mapping requires NameID in email format. After enabling SSO, local passwords are disabled for all non-admin users. SCIM provisioning can be layered on top of SSO for automated user lifecycle management.

title: SCIM provisioning setup
text: SCIM (System for Cross-domain Identity Management) automates user creation and deactivation. Generate a SCIM bearer token under Admin > Security > Provisioning. Fluxline implements SCIM 2.0 core schema; group push is supported for Okta and Entra ID. Deprovisioned users retain their audit history but lose all active sessions within five minutes.

title: Deploying agents in a private VPC
text: For private-network sources, deploy the Fluxline agent inside your VPC. The agent makes outbound-only connections; no inbound ports are required. Allocate at least 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM per agent. High-availability pairs are supported: two agents with the same pool ID load-balance automatically and fail over within 30 seconds.

title: Rate limits and error FLX-429
text: The Fluxline API enforces a limit of 600 requests per minute per workspace. Exceeding it returns FLX-429 with a Retry-After header. Batch endpoints count as a single request regardless of payload size, so prefer batching over per-record calls. Sustained FLX-429 responses on sync jobs usually mean the schedule frequency should be reduced.

title: Snapshot vs incremental sync modes
text: Snapshot mode re-reads the full source on every run and is safest for small tables or sources without reliable change tracking. Incremental mode reads only changed records using a cursor column or CDC feed. Switching from snapshot to incremental requires one final snapshot run to establish the cursor baseline. Incremental mode reduces sync cost by 80-95% on large tables.

title: Data residency and regional storage
text: Workspace data is stored in the region selected at creation time: EU (Frankfurt), US (Virginia), or APAC (Singapore). Region cannot be changed after creation; migration requires a new workspace and a supported export. In-transit data always uses TLS 1.3. At-rest encryption uses AES-256 with keys rotated every 90 days.

title: Webhook delivery and retry policy
text: Webhooks are delivered at-least-once with exponential backoff: retries at 1, 5, 25, and 125 minutes, then the event is dead-lettered. A 2xx response within 10 seconds acknowledges delivery. Dead-lettered events remain replayable for 14 days from Admin > Events. Signature verification uses HMAC-SHA256 with the per-endpoint secret.

title: Error FLX-207: schema drift detected
text: FLX-207 is a warning raised when the source schema no longer matches the last mapped schema — for example a dropped column or a type change. Syncs continue for unaffected columns. Resolve by opening the mapping editor and accepting or rejecting each drift item. Auto-accept can be enabled per connector for additive changes only.

title: Billing: how MAR is calculated
text: Fluxline bills on Monthly Active Rows (MAR): the count of distinct source rows synced at least once in the billing month. Rows synced multiple times count once. Snapshot mode can inflate MAR on large tables — see the incremental sync guide. MAR usage is visible per connector under Admin > Billing > Usage, updated every six hours.

title: Exporting audit logs
text: Audit logs capture every admin action, login, and connector change with actor, timestamp, and source IP. Logs are retained for 400 days on all plans. Export options: CSV download (up to 90 days per export), scheduled delivery to an S3 bucket, or streaming via the audit webhook. SIEM integrations are documented for Splunk and Sentinel.

title: Agent upgrade procedure
text: Agents auto-upgrade by default during the workspace maintenance window. To pin a version, set auto_upgrade: false in agent.yaml — pinned agents older than 90 days lose connectivity to new connector types. Manual upgrade: download the installer, stop the service, replace binaries, restart. HA pairs upgrade one member at a time with no sync downtime.

title: Troubleshooting slow syncs
text: Slow syncs have three usual causes. First, snapshot mode on large tables — switch to incremental. Second, undersized agents — check CPU saturation on the agent host. Third, source-side throttling — many SaaS sources cap API reads; stagger schedules to avoid parallel jobs hitting the same source. The per-job timing breakdown under Job Details shows read, transform, and write phases separately.
